title: Launch cadence constraint mapper and KPI decision tree
content:
Purpose:
This working doc is a lightweight, operational playbook combining a constraint-mapper for launch cadence decisions and an actionable KPI decision tree. It is intended for product-ops, oncall, release engineers, and PMs to quickly triage go/no-go choices during preflight and early rollout windows.

Context and scope:
- Applies to feature launches that materially change inference traffic patterns (new endpoints, model swaps, batching changes, quantization flips) or routing policies across hosted/dedicated/private.
- Focus: readiness signals that should block, delay, or de-scope a launch; mapping constraints to mitigation; and a compact KPI-driven decision tree for operational calls.
- Not a replacement for the full launch playbook — this is the rapid triage lens to use inside the first 48h of a rollout.

How to use the cadence constraint mapper (quick):
1) Populate the top section (Feature, Owner, Target date, Traffic plan, Primary risk bucket).
2) Run the preflight checklist (section below) with owners present. Mark each red/yellow/green.
3) Walk the KPI decision tree if any red signals present — escalate per tree outcome.
4) If go-ahead, enable phased rollout with the surge buckets described in the Capacity Roulette section.

Constraint categories (definitions):
- Capacity: GPU count, reserved queues, burst lanes, autoscale headroom.
- Latency SLO: p95 and p99 for synchronous endpoints, end-to-end quantile targets.
- Cost/Economics: expected per-1k-token cost delta, burst spend ceiling.
- Quality/regression: eval delta on core test prompts (automated baseline comparisons).
- Dependency: infra (K8s config/VM images), data pipelines, billing, compliance approvals.
- Observability: tracing enabled, token-level cost breakdown, alert routes configured.

KPI decision tree (textual walkthrough):
- Node A: Are p95 latency and error rate within target on staging under 2x projected production concurrency? (check A1/A2)
  - If yes -> Node B.
  - If no -> Block launch unless mitigation A-mitigations implemented (reduce batch size, enable cache prefixing, fallback to smaller model).
- Node B: Is quality regression <= allowed delta (example: ROUGE/embedding-sim delta <= 2%) on canary prompts?
  - If yes -> Node C.
  - If no -> Block until model fallback or prompt-adjust heuristics applied; schedule rapid eval loop.
- Node C: Is projected cost delta within the committed budget for first 30d (per-tenant or org-level)?
  - If yes -> Node D (gradual rollout).
  - If no -> Consider gated rollout to 5% users + cost throttle, or sign-off from Finance for overage.
- Node D: Observability and oncall readiness: are alerts and playbooks wired to correct Slack/rotation?
  - If yes -> Proceed to phased rollout.
  - If no -> Delay until alerting and runbooks are in place; if rollout must proceed, require triage pod in first 48h.

Decision thresholds (examples to set at launch planning):
- p95 <= 250ms for critical endpoints, p99 <= 800ms (adjust per feature).
- Error rate (5xx) < 0.5% sustained over 10m window.
- Eval quality regression < 2 percentage points on primary metric or embeddings mean-sim >= 0.95 of baseline.
- Cost delta <= 20% of prior monthly spend for the feature area (or explicit budget signoff).

Roadmap tracker snapshot (tabular text for quick copy into a sheet):
- Feature: "Streaming response backpressure improvements" | Owner: "Laura Chen" | Target Q: 2025-Q4 | Dependencies: infra-autoscale, tracing-v2 | Risk score: 6/10 | Mitigation: pre-warm pool + canary.
- Feature: "Model quantization rollout (int8)" | Owner: "Samir Patel" | Target Q: 2025-Q4 | Dependencies: quant-kernels, per-tenant opt-outs | Risk score: 7/10 | Mitigation: fallback variant + telemetry hooks.
- Feature: "Route-by-cost policy" | Owner: "Evelyn Martinez" | Target Q: 2026-Q1 | Dependencies: billing-alloc, policy-engine | Risk score: 5/10 | Mitigation: staged traffic + synthetic traffic tests.

Preflight readiness checklist (run within 7d and within 24–48h prior to gated rollout):
- [ ] Feature spec in product-ops tracker with owners, rollback plan, and traffic plan.
- [ ] Canary evaluation harness defined and passing baseline control.
- [ ] Load tests run at 2x projected production concurrency with no p95 violations in staging.
- [ ] Observability: tracing, token-cost breakdown, and route dashboards exist and are accessible.
- [ ] Alerting: alert definitions mapped to channel and escalation path; runbook present.
- [ ] Compliance/legal signoffs (if PII, data region constraints) documented.
- [ ] Billing/finance informed if expected spend > $X (org threshold).
- [ ] Customer success notified for beta customers and opt-in/out list prepared.

Go / No-Go quick matrix (for leads at T-0):
- Green: all checks green -> proceed with 10% canary (24h) -> expand by factor if metrics stable.
- Yellow: one non-critical item yellow -> require triage pod, reduce canary to 1-2% and extend observation window to 72h.
- Red: any blocking item (quality regression, p99 violations, missing critical alerting) -> hold launch.

Owner heatmap (who to call first by risk area):
- Capacity/GPU autoscale: Noah Greene (eng-infra)
- Latency & Serving runtime: Samir Patel (serving-runtime)
- Model quality / evals: Dr. Priya Anand (applied-ml)
- Billing / Cost: Mina Lopez (finance)
- Compliance / Private deploys: Evelyn Martinez (product-security)
- Oncall & incident runbooks: Laura Chen (product-ops)

Capacity Roulette (simulation method for surge probability):
- Purpose: inexpensive randomized stress runs across launch window to reveal brittle autoscale thresholds and dependency failures that deterministic tests miss.
- Method: create 5 short bursts (30–90s) at random offsets during a 48h canary window. Each burst ramps at different shapes: linear, sawtooth, step, spike, and sustained.
- Instruments to watch: queue length, pod spinup time, GPU utilization, token cost anomaly, trace sampling rate.
- Triage triggers: any sustained queue rise > 3x baseline for > 60s without autoscale response -> mark capacity red and execute pre-warm mitigation.

Playbook snippets (short runbook for first 60m incident):
1) Assess: check pine metrics (p50/p95/p99), error rate, and recent deploys.
2) Decide mitigation: scale up pre-warmed pool OR flip fallback model route.
3) Action owner: infra to scale, serving runtime to flip route, product-ops to notify CS and PM.
4) Postmortem trigger: if customer-facing errors > 0.1% for 1h or SLA breach.

Notes / open questions for next sync:
- Should we unify cost thresholds across hosted and dedicated or keep per-deployment policies? (decision needed by 2025-11-30).
- Do we want an automated gating job that evaluates the KPI decision tree and gives a green/yellow/red badge in the console before rollout? (proto risk: downstream automation false positives).

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Laura: convert the roadmap snapshot into the shared sheet and request Finance signoff for quant rollout (due 2025-11-25).
- Samir: schedule two randomized Capacity Roulette runs in staging before 2025-11-18.
- Evelyn: finalize compliance checklist for private deploys by 2025-11-22.

Appendix: quick glossary
- Capacity Roulette: randomized short-burst stress testing across a canary window.
- Canary prompt set: the curated list of prompts used for quality/regression evaluation for a feature.
- Pre-warm pool: kept-idle GPU instances ready to accept immediate traffic without cold-start.

Document history: created 2025-10-02 by Laura Chen; iterated with Samir and Evelyn during Q4 readiness reviews.

-- end of working doc (copy into a formal playbook once final)
